transcript.text: Hi, we've just had a Bosch KGN36VLEAG delivered last week and it makes a gurgling, bubbling sound like water running, plus a click every so often and a crack noise at night. Is it faulty? It's driving my husband mad.

The good news is that all three noises you describe are normal for this model, especially in the first few weeks. The KGN36VLEAG is a NoFrost fridge freezer, and these designs tend to be a bit more audible than older ones.

## What each sound is

Gurgling, bubbling, or running water
This is the refrigerant flowing through the pipes as it changes between liquid and gas. It's often most noticeable just after the compressor starts or stops. It's completely normal and is often louder in a new appliance while the system settles.

Occasional clicking
This is usually the thermostat or control system switching the compressor on or off, or the internal air damper or fan starting and stopping. A click every so often is expected.

Cracking or creaking (especially at night)
This is the plastic inner lining expanding and contracting with temperature changes. NoFrost models also run an automatic defrost cycle, which warms things slightly and then cools them again, causing those cracks and pops. You notice it more at night simply because the house is quieter.

## Things that can make it quieter

• Check it's level. Adjust the front feet so it doesn't rock. An unlevel fridge can amplify noises.
• Give it space. Make sure it isn't touching the wall, cupboards, or other appliances, and that pipes at the back aren't touching each other or the cabinet.
• Check inside. Bottles, jars, or shelves touching each other can rattle or vibrate.
• Floor type. Hard floors and kitchens with lots of hard surfaces reflect sound more.
• Give it time. Many people find the noises become less noticeable after 2 to 4 weeks, partly because the appliance settles and partly because you get used to it.

## When it might actually be a fault

Contact Bosch if you notice:
• Loud buzzing, humming, grinding, or knocking
• Repeated clicking every few minutes with the fridge not getting cold (this can mean the compressor is failing to start)
• The compressor running constantly without stopping
• Water leaking, ice building up, or temperatures not holding

It comes with a 2-year Bosch guarantee, so if you're still unsure, you can book a check through Bosch UK customer service or their website at no cost under warranty.

From what you've described, though, it sounds like a perfectly healthy new fridge doing its thing. Hopefully that puts your husband's mind at rest!
